title: Famous Temples in India: A Region-by-Region Guide for Visitors
seoTitle: Famous Temples in India: A Region-by-Region Guide | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: India's famous temples region by region, from Kashi Vishwanath and Kedarnath to Meenakshi, Tirumala, Jagannath, Konark and Khajuraho, with UNESCO sites and tips.
description: A region-by-region guide to India's famous temples for visitors: living pilgrimage temples such as Kashi Vishwanath, Tirumala, Meenakshi and Jagannath, UNESCO-listed temples such as Brihadeeswarar, Khajuraho, Konark, Hampi, Pattadakal, Ramappa and the Hoysala temples, temple architecture styles, dress codes and entry rules.
dek: India's temples range from busy pilgrimage shrines to thousand-year-old masterpieces of stone. Here is where to find the best known, region by region.

hero.alt: A painted gopuram of the Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu

intro: India has two kinds of famous temple, and many are both. Living pilgrimage temples such as Tirumala, Kashi Vishwanath or Jagannath in Puri draw daily crowds for darshan. Historic temples such as Konark, Khajuraho or the Chola temples of Thanjavur are celebrated as architecture, and several are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Styles differ by region: the curved Nagara towers of the north, the Dravida gopurams and vimanas of the south, the Kalinga temples of Odisha and the star-shaped Hoysala temples of Karnataka. This guide groups the best-known temples by region, with links to our detailed guides.
quickAnswer: India's most famous temples include Kashi Vishwanath (Varanasi), Kedarnath and Badrinath (Uttarakhand), Somnath and Dwarkadhish (Gujarat), Jagannath (Puri), Tirumala Venkateswara (Andhra Pradesh), Meenakshi (Madurai), Ramanathaswamy (Rameswaram) and Guruvayur (Kerala). UNESCO-listed temples include Brihadeeswarar at Thanjavur, Khajuraho, Konark, Hampi, Pattadakal, Mahabalipuram, Ramappa and the Hoysala temples of Belur and Halebidu.
takeaways: Living pilgrimage temples and historic monument temples are both worth visiting, with different rules.
Several temples, including Brihadeeswarar, Khajuraho, Konark and Hampi, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Some temples admit only Hindus, and many southern temples have strict dress codes.
Nagara, Dravida, Kalinga and Hoysala styles make each region's temples distinctive.
October to March is the most comfortable time to visit most temple towns.

sections.heading: Dress codes and entry rules
list: Many south Indian temples ask men to wear a dhoti or mundu and remove shirts, and women to wear sarees or long traditional dress; examples include Padmanabhaswamy in Thiruvananthapuram and Guruvayur.
Some temples, including Jagannath in Puri, Guruvayur and Padmanabhaswamy, admit only Hindus.
Phones, cameras and bags are often not allowed inside; use the cloakrooms.
Monument temples run by the ASI have tickets and fixed hours; living temples follow ritual timings.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Follow each temple's dress code and entry rules; check them before you travel.
Keep valuables secure in crowded temple towns.
Hire guides only from official counters at monument sites.
packing: Traditional clothes for southern temples (dhoti or mundu; saree or long dress)
Slip-on footwear and socks for hot floors
A small bag without leather for Jain temples
Water and a hat for monument sites

faqs.q: Which is the most famous temple in India?
faqs.a: Several are equally famous: Kashi Vishwanath, Tirumala, the Jagannath Temple in Puri and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai are among the best known.

faqs.q: Which Indian temples are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
faqs.a: Among them are the Brihadeeswarar and other Chola temples, Khajuraho, Konark, Hampi, Pattadakal, Mahabalipuram, Ramappa, the Hoysala temples and Ellora.

faqs.q: Do Indian temples have a dress code?
faqs.a: Many do, especially in the south, where traditional dress is required at temples such as Padmanabhaswamy and Guruvayur.
No. Some temples, including Jagannath in Puri, admit only Hindus; check each temple's rules.

faqs.q: What are the main temple architecture styles?
faqs.a: Nagara in the north, Dravida in the south, Kalinga in Odisha and the Hoysala style in Karnataka, among others.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit temple towns?
faqs.a: October to March for most of India; summer for the Himalayan shrines.
